sampling_model.design: Two randomized regime studies report complete \(2\times2\) tables, one under \(\operatorname{do}(Z=0)\) and one under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0)\).
sampling_model.units: The population version treats \(A\) and \(B\) as exact laws of one SCM; the optional sampling result uses multinomial frequency tables of sizes \(nA\) and \(nB\).
sampling_model.treatment: The first regime fixes \(Z=0\) and leaves \(X\) natural; the second fixes \(X=0\) and leaves \(Z\) natural.
sampling_model.overlap: Strict positivity of all eight population cells implies \(0<p,r<1\), \(0<a<p\), and \(0<b<r\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance functions are estimated. The optional interval uses only empirical multinomial cells and simultaneous concentration.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Minimization or maximization of the produced polynomial program gives sharp lower or upper bounds on the declared target.
Counterfactual consistency of overlapping categorical marginal SCMs restricts the admissible marginal and joint SCMs.
Every categorical SCM has a finite canonical SCM with the same graph and all the same counterfactual distributions.
EMCC returns fully specified compatible SCMs whose counterfactual range approximates the actual bounds from inside.
The global extrema of a response-function linear program occur at vertices of its feasible polytope.

body.tldr: Two complete experiments on overlapping margins of a binary collider need not arise from one SCM. Under two mutually independent shared roots and private outcome noise, the proposal seeks an iff compatibility inequality and a closed-form sharp interval for the all-zero joint-intervention risk. The decisive open step is a common finite threshold extension that preserves both source independence and one deterministic outcome law. Its resolution yields constant-time endpoints, exact rational endpoint certificates, a positive boundary regression case, and a conservative optional sampling interval, all for this fixed graph only.

project_justification.gap: General discrete-SCM methods can optimize this query numerically, and causal-marginal methods explain why overlapping reports must be consistent, but neither checked line supplies the graph-specific compatibility frontier, analytic endpoints, or a small common-SCM witness.
project_justification.niche: The fixed binary collider collapses to four natural-treatment strata, yet source independence prevents the armwise completions and unrestricted latent couplings used in simpler partial-identification arguments.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the two-mass fiber, resolves its source-preserving finite extension, and packages the resulting iff test and max/min interval as an exact certificate procedure for the same input handled generically by Autobounds.

body.related_work: Gresele et al. formulate the structural causal marginal problem and show how one shared response-function law constrains overlapping causal models; their main analytic Boolean construction is causally sufficient, while their confounded extension retains a high-dimensional partially factorized law. Duarte et al. prove that discrete causal bounds under observational and experimental evidence reduce to sharp polynomial programs and implement this result in Autobounds; that general theorem informs the present specialization but is not claimed to be tightened. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim prove finite canonical SCM sufficiency for arbitrary categorical counterfactual distributions; the proposed at-most-eight-point private extension is a menu-specific certificate, not a new generic canonicalization theorem. Sachs, Jonzon, Sjoelander, and Gabriel derive tight symbolic bounds for response-function models whose constraints are linear; their elimination logic motivates the four-stratum analysis, while the independent latent-source structure here must be preserved explicitly. Zaffalon et al. fuse heterogeneous observational and randomized studies through causal EM and report approximate inner ranges; their work is adjacent rather than a theorem-level target. Shridharan and Iyengar reduce the degree of multilinear causal-bound programs in quasi-Markovian graphs, but do not state a closed-form solution for this experimental menu. Finkelstein and Shpitser derive inequalities from logical relations among counterfactual events, and Balke and Pearl provide the foundational response-type sharp-bound template for binary instrumental variables; neither checked example matches this collider target.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The reduction to \((c,d)\) and denominator-eight enumerations are diagnostic evidence only. The universal source-preserving extension must still verify one common deterministic \(fY\), one private root \(W0\), both complete experimental tables, and mutual independence of \(U0,V0,W0\). A correlated-root model can escape the claimed independent-source interval, so replacing the product law by an unrestricted response simplex is invalid.
body.honest_scope: The compatibility algebra and endpoint projection are the tractable portion; the finite common extension is explicitly open and load-bearing. Structural zeros, correlated or budget-dependent shared roots, different study populations, all four joint-intervention risks, three or more parents, minimal support, nominal tie-robust inference, general compilation, and any field-tier claim are excluded. If regime \(B\) is omitted, the same mass accounting collapses to the standard missing-stratum bound \(q\in[a,a+1-p]\); symmetrically, omitting regime \(A\) gives \(q\in[b,b+1-r]\). As a second sanity case, the positive boundary tables in \(\text{prop:boundary-kill-test}\) pin \(c\) while leaving the nondegenerate interval \([3/8,5/8]\), so compatibility does not silently become point identification.
